title: Binary Search: Interval Conventions, Boundary Updates, and Applicability
evidence_note: The supplied fixture (fixture_binary_search_en) explicitly covers closed and half-open interval conventions, midpoint computation, boundary updates, termination conditions, complexity, and applicability constraints, which is sufficient for one easy multiple-choice question.
learning_objectives: Explain the closed-interval [left, right] convention used by binary search, including its initial boundaries and termination condition.
Identify the correct midpoint computation and boundary update rules for an exact-match search on a sorted ascending array.

questions.stem: According to the supplied notes, in the closed-interval binary search on an ascending array with distinct values and zero-based indexing, which statement correctly describes the interval convention and its boundary updates?
options: The interval [left, right] is initially [0, n - 1]; the loop runs while left <= right; a middle value smaller than the target sets left = mid + 1, and a larger one sets right = mid - 1.
The interval [left, right] is initially [0, n]; the loop runs while left < right; a middle value smaller than the target sets left = mid, and a larger one sets right = mid.
The interval [left, right) is initially [0, n]; the loop runs while left <= right; a middle value smaller than the target sets left = mid + 1, and a larger one sets right = mid.
The interval [left, right] is initially [0, n - 1]; the loop runs while left < right; a middle value smaller than the target sets left = mid + 1, and a larger one sets right = mid.
questions.explanation: The notes state that a closed search interval [left, right] contains every eligible position, starts with left = 0 and right = n - 1, loops while left <= right, and updates left = mid + 1 when the middle value is smaller and right = mid - 1 when it is larger. Option B and C describe half-open behavior, and option D mixes the closed initial boundaries with the half-open loop condition.
questions.difficulty_reason: This is an easy item because it asks the student to directly recall and explain one clearly stated knowledge point from the notes: the closed-interval convention with its initial boundaries, loop condition, and boundary updates. The conditions are complete and no complex strategy selection is required.

expected_steps: Recall that the closed interval starts as [0, n - 1] and loops while left <= right.
Recall that a smaller middle value sets left = mid + 1 and a larger one sets right = mid - 1.

visual_prompt: A horizontal array of sorted distinct values with a highlighted closed interval [left, right], a midpoint marker, and arrows showing the two possible boundary updates: left moves to mid + 1 or right moves to mid - 1.
